name: Giza Plateau: what you are walking on
note: Orientation: three kings (Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure, 4th Dynasty c. 2600-2500 BC), each with pyramid + mortuary temple + causeway + valley temple + queens' pyramids + cemeteries of officials; the Sphinx; the order to walk; tickets (plateau vs interior); the camel/horse hustle; the panorama point.

name: The Great Pyramid of Khufu
note: 146.6 m original (138.5 today), 2.3 million blocks, 20-27 years, tallest man-made structure for 3,800 years; precision of base and orientation; casing stones; the entrance vs the forced 'robbers' tunnel' of al-Ma'mun (820 AD); the 2017 muon 'Big Void'.

name: Inside the Great Pyramid: Grand Gallery and King's Chamber
note: The climb: descending passage, ascending passage, Grand Gallery (8.6 m high corbelled), King's Chamber with granite sarcophagus too big for the passage, relieving chambers with Khufu's workgang graffiti, 'air shafts', Queen's Chamber and Gantenbrink's 'door'. Practical: heat, stoop, no photos rules may apply.

name: Khufu's queens' pyramids and the Eastern Cemetery
note: Three satellite pyramids east of the Great Pyramid for queens Hetepheres(?), Meritites and Henutsen; the tiny cult pyramid found 1991; the royal family mastabas (Kawab, Meresankh, Khufukhaf); the Hetepheres shaft G7000X.

name: Tomb of Queen Meresankh III
commons: Meresankh III tomb Giza statues rock cut
note: Rock-cut chapel in the Eastern Cemetery with vivid painted reliefs and a row of ten rock-cut female statues; Meresankh granddaughter of Khufu, wife of Khafre, daughter of Hetepheres II; 'bought' by her mother; the black granite sarcophagus. Worth the separate ticket.

name: The Western Cemetery: city of the officials
note: Grid of mastabas (Arabic for bench) laid out like a town for Khufu's officials: Hemiunu the architect (G4000), Iymery, Nesutnefer; the Reisner/Junker excavations; what a mastaba contains (chapel, false door, serdab, shaft).

name: Hemiunu, the man who built the Great Pyramid
note: Vizier and 'overseer of all the king's works', nephew of Khufu, huge mastaba G4000 near the Great Pyramid; his fat seated statue (Hildesheim) with the eyes gouged by robbers; what the job involved.

name: Tomb of Seshemnefer IV (near the Sphinx)
note: Late 5th/6th Dynasty mastaba south of Khufu's causeway, often open and free: pillared portico, offering scenes, false doors; good to see what an Old Kingdom chapel looks like.

name: Pyramid of Khafre
note: 136.4 m, looks taller because built on higher ground; the surviving Tura limestone casing at the top; Belzoni's entry in 1818 and his graffito in the burial chamber; two entrances; the granite sarcophagus with a bull's bones.

name: Valley Temple of Khafre
commons: Valley Temple of Khafre granite pillars
note: Best-preserved Old Kingdom temple: monolithic red granite pillars and calcite floor; where Mariette found the diorite Khafre statue in a pit (1860); 23 statue emplacements; purification/embalming theories; the causeway up to the pyramid.

name: Khafre's mortuary temple and causeway
note: Ruined but shows the standard plan (entrance hall, court, statue niches, storerooms, sanctuary); the 494 m causeway; the first appearance of the 'five statue niches'. Short.

name: Pyramid of Menkaure
note: 65 m, granite casing on the lower 16 courses, unfinished dressing; the vertical gash from Saladin's son al-Aziz Uthman's demolition attempt in 1196 (gave up after 8 months); Vyse found the basalt sarcophagus (lost at sea 1838); the Menkaure triads and dyad from the valley temple.

name: Menkaure's three queens' pyramids
note: Short. One true pyramid and two step pyramids; Khamerernebty II; good photo spot with the three big ones behind.

name: The Great Sphinx
note: 73 m long, carved from a limestone knoll left by quarrying; whose face (Khafre vs Khufu/Djedefre debate); the missing nose (not Napoleon: Sa'im al-Dahr 1378 or earlier), the beard fragments (BM/Cairo); 'Horemakhet'; sand burials and restorations; erosion and the water-erosion fringe theory; Thutmose IV's Dream Stele between the paws.

name: The Dream Stele of Thutmose IV
note: Granite stela between the paws: the prince fell asleep in the Sphinx's shadow, it promised him the throne if he cleared the sand; political propaganda for a younger son; made from a reused door lintel of Khafre's temple.

name: The Sphinx Temple
note: Short. Old Kingdom temple directly in front of the Sphinx, built from blocks quarried from around the Sphinx itself; 24 pillars (hours of the day?), two sanctuaries east and west for sunrise and sunset; never finished, no inscriptions.

name: Tomb of Khentkawes I, the 'fourth pyramid'
note: Short. Huge two-stepped tomb on a rock outcrop near Menkaure's valley temple; 'mother of two kings of Upper and Lower Egypt'; her town of priests' houses alongside; bridge from the 4th to the 5th Dynasty.

name: The pyramid builders: workers' town and cemetery
commons: Giza workers cemetery tombs pyramid builders
note: Not slaves: Mark Lehner's Heit el-Ghurab 'Lost City' with bakeries, breweries, barracks, cattle bones (meat for workers); Zahi Hawass's workers' cemetery with healed fractures and titles; the rotating crews (phyles) named like 'Friends of Khufu'; beer and bread rations.

name: How the pyramids were built
note: Quarrying with copper tools and dolerite pounders; Tura limestone casing across the river, Aswan granite 900 km by boat; ramps (straight, spiral, internal: Houdin); sledges on wet sand (2014 study); levelling with water; the Hatnub ramp with post-holes (2018); the Diary of Merer; no, not aliens: the evidence of quarry marks and graffiti.

name: The Diary of Merer: a Khufu foreman's logbook
note: Oldest inscribed papyri (2013, Wadi al-Jarf on the Red Sea, Tallet): inspector Merer's team ferrying limestone from Tura to 'Akhet Khufu', in year 27 of Khufu, under vizier Ankhhaf; what the logbook shows about logistics, canals and the Nile branch to Giza.

name: The boat pits around the Great Pyramid
aliases: where the solar boat was found
note: Five boat-shaped pits; the two sealed pits on the south side held the dismantled cedar ships now at GEM (seen 11 Oct); link back to the GEM entry; the smell of cedar when opened in 1954.

name: The panorama viewpoint
note: Short. The viewpoint south-west of Menkaure where all nine pyramids line up; where the 9 Pyramids Lounge/Khufu's restaurant sits; best light; the camel negotiation ritual.

name: Why a pyramid? What it meant
note: The primeval mound and the benben stone of Heliopolis; the sun's rays in stone; the king's ascent to join Ra and the circumpolar 'imperishable stars'; from Djoser's step pyramid to Sneferu's experiments (Meidum, Bent, Red) to Giza; why pyramid-building declined.
